### Common Causes of Elevated LFTs

- **Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD):** Formerly known as fatty liver disease, this happens when extra fat builds up in the liver and is frequently linked to insulin resistance, obesity, type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, or high blood pressure.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESswEBxCJF1930U_4av8JJFsoRdcqnFewdK8LHQ9un0DehuCGkmFk28d22LCbbFA6RfBvuyzrHG1fUquqaWGlDikPALPIO_75owbsNt-skF_SJQcmbfhp8nRc6KJluyAxYw09-JvaeAvaRbqERMVX5TpXyqwNTLxu5bfdMR_wQXT2f9z16rdZEE21KEiQsE6y0G7L-wVOolOXb0gAxoBaApSc1MLLygizLwoE0NneTakx7ZfEUNA)
- **Alcohol Use:** Heavy or long-term alcohol consumption (alcohol-related liver disease) or recent alcohol use can irritate and damage liver tissue.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF11UUdWYpVz7_2t1fCdwlSTsuQk50zI7c813ScHYpdJgqIlZCVE74MFaOZLf6U5TaRjiodj4-NlbDIZ0Yhl46tr7puZbbNhGjWOezM33s4E1-vZEn7isnaFGQ4YGDfSfSE1n6E_VmxFSr-Bl3svmVQSsqOujlWVsbXWyX_eG7zcFWyGY7jYDPGHvfkln0IQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESswEBxCJF1930U_4av8JJFsoRdcqnFewdK8LHQ9un0DehuCGkmFk28d22LCbbFA6RfBvuyzrHG1fUquqaWGlDikPALPIO_75owbsNt-skF_SJQcmbfhp8nRc6KJluyAxYw09-JvaeAvaRbqERMVX5TpXyqwNTLxu5bfdMR_wQXT2f9z16rdZEE21KEiQsE6y0G7L-wVOolOXb0gAxoBaApSc1MLLygizLwoE0NneTakx7ZfEUNA)
- **Medications and Supplements:** Over-the-counter and prescription drugs—most notably acetaminophen (Tylenol)—as well as statins, certain antibiotics, and herbal or dietary supplements can stress the liver.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF11UUdWYpVz7_2t1fCdwlSTsuQk50zI7c813ScHYpdJgqIlZCVE74MFaOZLf6U5TaRjiodj4-NlbDIZ0Yhl46tr7puZbbNhGjWOezM33s4E1-vZEn7isnaFGQ4YGDfSfSE1n6E_VmxFSr-Bl3svmVQSsqOujlWVsbXWyX_eG7zcFWyGY7jYDPGHvfkln0IQ)[[2]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UVco0M7mpqs&t=59)
- **Viral Hepatitis:** Infections such as Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C cause direct inflammation of the liver. Other viruses like Epstein-Barr virus (mononucleosis) or cytomegalovirus (CMV) can also trigger temporary elevations.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF11UUdWYpVz7_2t1fCdwlSTsuQk50zI7c813ScHYpdJgqIlZCVE74MFaOZLf6U5TaRjiodj4-NlbDIZ0Yhl46tr7puZbbNhGjWOezM33s4E1-vZEn7isnaFGQ4YGDfSfSE1n6E_VmxFSr-Bl3svmVQSsqOujlWVsbXWyX_eG7zcFWyGY7jYDPGHvfkln0IQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF17F64wAMqJEkHQthbkVTg8UktIlUt3cRMSy2mXMrw9mKJAfQcxqIioceymNS4FpFtwHqJoHR3lCHnBwPVqJSJbAB8aOwlhuZSNpbm1DftkrfFq6Pnznu1yX5-1NlDWauQhIk7dRbYNE7mC4hrQ0clIsFyQNg--CoI48rIekzD7rS6mOnumnkLZ3GxXR6np57)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=id2HhPLiA3o&t=438)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESzwEBxCJF115O4h_mGJB4G1EwsyTUv50LVaRWR1NTroVuYXMndswq44zdY-_rUXtoy_ukHHl4irQAfY9_OWS4Q_3pDKD4Gs1_-B4jL9Uf3hsma_8UCUA2_T40eGhhl0ELy1L3E_Kspe-8v4o089e05jGxSh2LOAePvVIBbZOMgsR9d0N5H3-Gjoito_kqMcl-7TZ1D6t55JrcMy5eBljHFv3taMivjmF27f3pzE_VZi_r5-wFCCUR7in-wDtIUIt9jKc0FSJhfaj55Zzoi0lz8LY)

- **Biliary or Other Conditions:** Gallbladder or bile duct issues (cholestatic patterns), heart failure, or severe systemic infections like sepsis can also elevate LFTs.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESkgEBxCJF11UUdWYpVz7_2t1fCdwlSTsuQk50zI7c813ScHYpdJgqIlZCVE74MFaOZLf6U5TaRjiodj4-NlbDIZ0Yhl46tr7puZbbNhGjWOezM33s4E1-vZEn7isnaFGQ4YGDfSfSE1n6E_VmxFSr-Bl3svmVQSsqOujlWVsbXWyX_eG7zcFWyGY7jYDPGHvfkln0IQ)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF17F64wAMqJEkHQthbkVTg8UktIlUt3cRMSy2mXMrw9mKJAfQcxqIioceymNS4FpFtwHqJoHR3lCHnBwPVqJSJbAB8aOwlhuZSNpbm1DftkrfFq6Pnznu1yX5-1NlDWauQhIk7dRbYNE7mC4hrQ0clIsFyQNg--CoI48rIekzD7rS6mOnumnkLZ3GxXR6np57)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXtrgPpv-O8l3sVBTNjcKeFgYaIKTKQmDoMsFl8VdxB2NQEFNu97s67GeBbAoLnK4ncb_e7tajU7XVVJBWlyOlsmclbk0QxItKM1zWulyatKW_F364yO_kiDEFS0yMcuE2pUXXFvUvoIje)

items.title: Common Causes of Elevated LFTs
items.text: Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD): Formerly known as fatty liver disease, this happens when extra fat builds up in the liver and is frequently linked to insulin resistance, obesity, type 2 diabetes, high cholesterol, or high blood pressure. Alcohol Use: Heavy or long-term alcohol consumption (alcohol-related liver disease) or recent alcohol use can irritate and damage liver tissue. Medications and Supplements: Over-the-counter and prescription drugs—most notably acetaminophen (Tylenol)—as well as statins, certain antibiotics, and herbal or dietary supplements can stress the liver. Viral Hepatitis: Infections such as Hepatitis A, Hepatitis B, and Hepatitis C cause direct inflammation of the liver. Other viruses like Epstein-Barr virus (mononucleosis) or cytomegalovirus (CMV) can also trigger temporary elevations. Autoimmune and Genetic Conditions: Autoimmune hepatitis (where the immune system attacks liver cells), hemochromatosis (iron overload), Wilson's disease (copper accumulation), and Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency can cause chronic enzyme spikes. Non-Liver (Extrahepatic) Causes: Strenuous exercise or muscle injury (which raises AST), celiac disease, thyroid disorders, or sample hemolysis (damage to blood cells during the lab draw) can mimic liver problems. Biliary or Other Conditions: Gallbladder or bile duct issues (cholestatic patterns), heart failure, or severe systemic infections like sepsis can also elevate LFTs.
